If your partner collects vinyl, this is one of those Christmas gift ideas they'll appreciate for years to come. Read our full review of the Sony PS-LX3BT.

Sources indicate that CDs are the latest retro tech to have a resurgence among Gen Z. Tracking down a cool old CD player on eBay will earn you a lot of cred, but if you don't want to go through the trouble, this see-through model from Retradisc looks really, really cool. It works with wired or wireless headphones, and best of all, it doesn't cost as much as Sony's fresh gold-plated Walkman.

Technics continues to make a strong impression in the wireless audio market. When it comes to hi-fi headphones, the new EAH-A1000 are a sonic stunner that put many category leaders to shame. They crush the AirPods Max 2 in most areas and rival the Sony WH-1000XM6 sound quality, while also outlasting both competitors in playtime (up to 45 hours per charge) and multi-point pairing. Plus, the elegant craftsmanship is a 10/10. Every audiophile should have this at the top of their wish list this year.

In a recent development, sonos has long been a go-to for WiFi speakers, but JBL’s newly introduced Cove Series is a true competitor that offers a compelling wireless audio experience at a more attainable price. If you have someone on your shopping list who loves music, the Cove speaker will fill up their bedroom, living room, or back patio with big sound.

Plus, it even offers automatic self-tuning, AI Sound Boost technology that optimizes audio for listening environments, and hands-free Alexa voice control.

Recent findings suggest that choosing a signature scent for your hubby isn’t as easy as picking out a video game; you need to know their olfactory preferences. If you’re unsure what they like — or shopping for someone especially particular — let them decide with one of Fulton & Roark’s discovery sets. The variety gives them a chance to explore different scents and narrow down their next go-to fragrance. (Pro tip: We like Palmetto and Ghost Trees.).

Recent findings suggest that harry’s has something for every man’s mug. Guys who prefer a clean-shaven look can reach for the brand’s shaving kit, which includes the popular Truman handle with secure grip and multiple five-blade cartridges that deliver close shaves. No-shave November devotees can keep their mane well-kempt with the beard wash and conditioning spray bundle.

In a recent development, every well-groomed gentleman deserves a luxury electric shaver in his life. The Panasonic Arc5 Pro is our pick for its comfortable, close shaves and flexible head, which is designed to improve cutting performance. It works for both wet and dry shaving, and the built-in pop-up trimmer provides seamless control and navigation to clean up edges around the neckline.

Recent findings suggest that we think the Mashable Choice Award-winning Shark CryoGlow is the best red light mask you can buy right now (and one of the best Christmas gifts for women). It provides more complete coverage than other masks from brands like OmniLux or CurrentBody, and each bulb can emit red, blue, or near-infrared light.

Former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart was convinced that the CryoGlow’s bacteria-killing blue light setting is what finally cleared a year’s worth of her relentless adult acne. Some cooling under-eye pads complete this luxurious self-care device. Read our full review of the Shark CryoGlow.

Sources indicate that several Mashable staffers use Shark's FlexStyle multi-styler on a regular basis. (Mangino did her wedding hair with it!) It costs half as much as Dyson's iconic Airwrap but works just as well, if not better. It supports a ton of different attachments and has a unique twisting base that functions like a regular hair dryer on its own. Read our full review of the Shark FlexStyle.

According to recent reports, the Playground is a cubic gaming console designed for playing family-friendly games with motion controls — no need for a traditional gamepad. Perry described it as "a spiritual successor to the old Xbox Kinect." If this is the first time you're hearing of it, get with the program: It managed to outsell the PlayStation 5 on Black Friday 2025, and was difficult to find in stock during the holiday season last year. If you proposal on gifting it within the coming weeks, we'd recommend adding it to your cart ASAP.

Fascinatingly, this squishy little toy is one of the hottest products of 2026. People have stormed stores and waited hours in line to buy them, and there's even a reselling market for them. Mashable's Mangino bought some before the hype and said they "promptly became coveted fidgets among our friends for their pleasing, pliable feel.".

According to recent reports, like wired earbuds, CD players, and other items from your childhood, Pokémon cards are so incredibly back — and dare we say, bigger than ever. The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is a giftable bundle that includes 9 booster packs and plenty of other goodies. Amazon is also selling it on an invite-only basis; try your luck because it's well under market price, as of this writing.

In a recent development, routine can give children structure and help them feel more secure. The Skylight Buddy guides kids through mornings, afternoons, and bedtime, while helping them develop healthy habits and independence. They can add and check off chores, events, and tasks. This digital calendar also functions as an alarm clock and nightlight, signaling wake-up and sleep times. Personalization features help families reinforce goals and daily commitments.

According to recent reports, we recently named the Toniebox 2 one of Mashable's Gifts of the Year in our guide to the top gifts for kids. The kid-famous Toniebox is a favorite of the moms and dads on the Mashable team. Whether you're shopping for your own child or trying to earn a reputation as the cool aunt or uncle, kids and parents alike love these screen-free storytelling devices.

Recent findings suggest that if your tyke already has a Toniebox, they can always use more Tonies — the little figures you put on top of the device to activate a new storytime. Bluey and Pokémon Tonies joined the party this year.

Recent findings suggest that another Mashable Gift of the Year winner, this portable screen-free audio player is a hit with the three kiddos of Nicole Cammorata, Mashable's director of special projects. "Compatible cards power up everything from chapter books and shorter stories to music and learning-based content," she wrote. For an incredibly sweet personalized gift, you can have grandparents, siblings, or friends record custom audio messages on blank Yoto cards.

Industry observers note that don't overthink (or overspend) trying to think of the perfect Christmas gifts for kids. Keep it simple and combine two things kids love — Bluey and slime. This slimy sand adds a bit more texture to the average slime, letting kids mold it in upcoming ways. Even better, you can pick it up for under $15, and still have the best gift under the tree.

Recent findings suggest that gifting a pair of the best Beats headphones is a sure bet for any fashion-forward music lover. Fans of over-ear headphones will appreciate the modular Beats 360, which features a customizable design with swappable ear cushions, IPX4 sweat resistance, pleasant sound, and strong ANC. True wireless conformists can utilize the sporty Powerbeats Pro 2 for exercise and leisure; the revamped earhook design is optimized for comfort and sound performance.

According to recent reports, looking for the best gifts under $100? The Camp Snap 2 is one of our top picks. This screenless digital camera has six built-in filters and super simple controls. To transfer its photos to your phone, all you need is a USB-C cable. Mangino brought a Camp Snap 2 on her Grecian honeymoon this past summer, "and now I have the sweetest photos to look back on," she said. Read our full review of the Camp Snap 2.

The merchandising gods are working their magic this holiday season in anticipation of the biggest MCU film yet: Avengers: Doomsday. Funko Pop has a tempting lineup of Marvel collectibles, including multiple versions of Doctor Doom, beloved X-Men characters, and a 10-inch jumbo Sentinel. Steve Rogers, Thor, Shang-Chi, and several other familiar faces round out the collection.

Industry observers note that if your teenager is allowed to watch TV in their room, upgrade their older set to the Mashable Choice Award-winning Hisense DécoTV. The 32-inch model "is compact enough to fit just about anywhere and simplistically chic enough to fit in with just about any decor," mentioned Stodart. It'll be perfect for their college dorm room when the time comes. As a bonus, it costs much less than Samsung's smallest The Frame TV. Read our full review of the Hisense DécoTV.

Recent findings suggest that no one's too old for Play-Doh anymore: This summer, the modeling clay brand released its first-ever collection of adult craft kits, Blooms by Play-Doh. Each one comes with colorful, scented Play-Doh sticks that they can press and shape into a pretty floral bouquet, plus finishing spray and a clear vase. For crafty types who have grown bored of Lego's Botanical builds, this is one of our favorite Christmas gift ideas.

Industry observers note that the new Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the best flip phone we've tested this year, and Mashable's Werth especially recommends it "for a stylish, on-trend young person." It's easy to hold in one hand, durable, and available in an extremely cute purpley-pink color. And while its camera setup isn't wildly impressive, it does take a mean selfie. Read our full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8.

Sources indicate that retro tech is having another moment. Last year, cassette players were everywhere; this year, Bluetooth CD players are joining the old-school wave (there are two in this gift guide). They’re a fun pick for Gen Alpha teens who love iPods, disposable cameras, and DVDs, and you can pair it with their favorite artists' latest albums.

The Fosi Audio Merak works as a portable and desktop CD player, with modern extras including Bluetooth, USB drive playback, and one-touch CD ripping.

Recent findings suggest that the best Christmas gift for a hostess with the mostest is a Ninja Slushi Twist. It makes delicious frozen cocktails, slushies, and milkshakes just as well as the original Ninja Slushi, but now it works faster, picks settings for you, and adds a second mixing canister. That's right: Two flavors at once, baby. It's "just plain fun, and will make your home the go-to for your friend group," stated Stodart, who gave it a Mashable Choice Award. Read our full review of the Ninja SLUSHi Twist.

Bless the tea sipper in your family with this flavorful collection of 18 premium blends that bring winter warmth and wellness. These loose-leaf teas come in plant-based sachets and are sourced from small-scale farmers. The assortment includes multiple varieties of black, green, mint, oolong, and white teas.

The viral Ninja Crispi and the upcoming Cosori Iconic have both earned the Mashable staff's collective seal of approval. Why those air fryers, you might ask? Not only do they crisp up food nicely, but they're free of plastics and forever chemicals. The compact Crispi is ideal for cooking single-serve meals and meal-prepping; its glass containers come with lids for storing your leftovers. The Cosori is a sleeker stainless steel model with a bigger basket and handy smart controls. Read our full review of the Cosori Iconic.

Industry observers note that A digital dosing cup with a precision scale for weighing beans before grinding is the gift every coffee drinker didn’t think they needed until now. The Subminimal Subscale powers on quickly and features a hidden LED display for easy-to-read measurements. It can handle hot and cold liquids, and its minimalist design complements modern kitchen counters.

Recent findings suggest that the upcoming Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iPhone owners, in our opinion. It has a faster processor, pretty new ceramic finish options, and an improved heart sensor array. Mashable senior editor Stan Schroeder has been testing it this fall, and he stated the latter is "the star of the show" because it "allows for far more frequent measurements." It also "opens the door for new apps such as Readiness and an overhauled Vitals app," he added.

Industry observers note that we loved the Google Fitbit Air when we first tested it, and love it even more after the latest patch, which supports automatic detection for up to 100 sports and tracks blood pressure trends. It excels as both a fitness tracker and sleep tracker, making it a superb gift that athletes won’t ever take off. Not to mention it’s way more affordable than the Apple Watch Series 12, Oura Ring 5, and Whoop MG. Read our full review of the Fitbit Air.

Sources indicate that almost everyone on Mashable's shopping team owns an Owala FreeSip, which Mangino dubbed the "best water bottle ever." The 24-ounce insulated stainless steel bottle is designed to accommodate both sipping (via straw) and good ol' fashioned gulp when tipped back. For athletes, college students, teenagers, or anyone who drinks water, we think a colorful Owala is one of the best Christmas gifts under $50. Read our full review of the Owala FreeSip.

Mashable tech reporter Matt Binder, a self-proclaimed "longtime soccer dad," tested the new XbotGo Falcon sports tracking camera for an entire youth soccer season this year. His verdict: It's "a smart pick for parents and coaches." Its footage is sharp, you can monitor it in real time from your smartphone, and it works with nine different sports (soon to be 12). It's a bit of a splurge, but unlike a lot of the competition, it doesn't require a subscription. Read our full review of the XbotGo Falcon.

Tossing the football is a holiday tradition for many sports-loving households. This year, rifle this waterproof football into your dad’s chest. Dime Labs cleverly designed its footballs with silicone grip strips for better handling, and a woven microfiber cover to survive the wettest conditions. It comes in two sizes – 10.5 inches and 8.5 inches – with the smaller version well-suited to kids practicing their quarterback skills.

Sources indicate that it's a cooler. It's a boombox. It's both! We love the Igloo KoolTunes for its old-school design and surprisingly good audio quality. While it lacks deep bass, it offers clear, balanced sound and can get quite loud. "It's not a gimmick, but a fun fusion of summer party gear," said Mashable's Henschel. Read our full review of the Igloo KoolTunes.

The new Shark ChillPill is another Mashable Gift of the Year winner. It's a powerful portable fan that stands out for its swappable misting and cooling plate attachments, long battery life, and fun colorways. (Justin Bieber's SKYLRK brand teamed up with Shark for a limited-edition "Heat" variant, which is long sold out.) It came in clutch for Mangino on some of the hottest days of the summer. Read our full review of the Shark ChillPill.

Recent findings suggest that the LifeStraw is a Black Friday classic that always goes on sale around the holidays, which also makes it a perfect stocking stuffer for people who love camping and the great outdoors. You can stick one end of this straw into virtually any water source — no matter how gross — and clean, filtered water comes out the other end.

Portable Bluetooth speakers are crowd-pleasing gifts for just about anyone, from teenagers to parents, siblings, and friends. This year, we're loving the all-latest Tribit StormBox Micro 3. It produces satisfying sound in a compact design, is fully waterproof, and comes in multiple standout colorways. Tribit’s speaker is travel-friendly, with a magnetic snap that can latch onto fridge doors or bike handles.

Simply put, Yeti's stainless steel Rambler tumblers are crowd-pleasers. They're dishwasher-safe, incredibly durable, condensation-resistant, and available in a huge rainbow of colors and patterns. Pro tip: For a very affordable personalized Christmas gift, you can customize a Rambler with your own text, graphics, and logos on the Yeti website.

Power stations can come in handy in lots of unexpected situations. From camping at music festivals to charging up your phone in an emergency blackout, these lightweight and portable devices keep you on the grid. Bluetti makes some of our favorite power stations, and the Elite 30 V2 is a good starter model.

In a recent development, the AirFly Pro is a cult-favorite Bluetooth adapter that makes seatback screens on older planes compatible with wireless headphones. After using it on round-trip flights between Chicago and London, Henschel said she'd "never fly without it again." The newer AirFly Pro 2 has simpler controls, improved sound quality, and pairs faster. Read our full review of the Twelve South AirFly Pro.

Traveling abroad this winter? Take this handy adapter along. Anker’s latest travel charger works with outlets in nearly every country and can charge up to four devices at once. The voltage detection system monitors voltage, power output, and temperature in real time. All readings and charging statuses are displayed on the LCD screen.

Travel jewelry cases are both thoughtful and practical, and we like this one in particular. The velvet box comes in a few different colors, and it ensures your wife, girlfriend, or daughter's favorite rings, necklaces, and earrings never get misplaced when she's away from home. If you're hunting for one of the best Christmas gifts for women under $25, look no further.

Sources indicate that cushy ANC headphones are a non-negotiable for long travel days, and lead shopping reporter Bethany Allard thinks the latest Bose QuietComforts are the best mid-range option for flying. When she wore them on a plane, "I heard minimal engine hum and was able to completely tune out conversations from my fellow passengers," she wrote. "I also never felt the need to remove the headphones due to wear fatigue." Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort headphones (2nd Gen).

Nori’s garment steamers are a lifesaver for business travelers and fashion professionals. The Cloud Max makes de-wrinkling clothes a breeze, using gentle vacuum suction to pull fabric taut for smoother results. Anti-spit technology prevents leaks and water spots, and the steamer’s portable design fits comfortably in any travel bag.

Sources indicate that A weekender bag bridges the gap between a backpack and a suitcase. It should hold a few outfits, toiletries, and an extra pair of shoes for a two- or three-day trip. Quince’s Voyage bag fits the bill with a dedicated shoe compartment, multiple pockets, and a padded shoulder strap. It’s at the moment on sale for half of its original price, while supplies last.

Recent findings suggest that timothy Beck Werth is the Tech Editor at Mashable, where he leads coverage and assignments for the Tech and Shopping verticals. Tim has over 15 years of experience as a journalist and editor, and he has particular experience covering and testing consumer technology, smart home gadgets, and men’s grooming and style products. Uber began as a modern alternative to taxis, letting riders order through a phone app, track the driver’s route in real time, share their location with contacts, and even split the fare in the app—it was the convenience-obsessed answer to the old way of hailing cabs. Then in 2014, Uber leveled up with Uber Eats. Much like Uber was the convenient, modern answer to taxis, Uber Eats was the equivalent for food delivery.

Instead of calling a local restaurant and enlisting a delivery driver from that restaurant, Uber Eats draws from hundreds of participating restaurants, cafes, and stores in your area, tailoring deals and picks to your location and preferences. So if you want fresh sushi from your favorite local spot for a date night in, or just need some Advil and Gatorade after a night out, Uber Eats delivers the goods in minutes flat. Whether you’re newly introduced to the service or a longtime devotee, we have an Uber Eats promo code and other Uber Eats coupon codes to help you save substantial—and stay at home.

According to recent reports, one of the easiest ways to save big on Uber Eats is to create a fresh account. First-time Uber customers can save 30 to 50% on their first order, plus new offers with up to $20 off rides or $15 off Uber Eats orders. You don’t even need an Uber Eats promo code to get this steep discount—this offer applies automatically when you create your account and book your first trip or delivery. Use Uber Eats promo code US36J5H to get $15 off your first order.

Industry observers note that if you use the rideshare app often or order takeout multiple nights a week, an Uber One membership will pay for itself within a few weeks. At $10 per month, it offers major perks that add up over time if you use the service frequently. You’ll get tons of perks across rides and food delivery, including $0 delivery fees on eligible food, grocery, and retail orders, up to 10% off eligible Uber Eats orders, 5% back in Uber One credits on eligible rides, and automatic surge savings. Uber One members save $29 on average every month.

As mentioned above, the simplest way to save big with Uber is to be a first-time user. You’ll save 30 to 50% on your first ride, including up to $20 off all rides or $15 off Uber Eats orders. You don’t even need an Uber promo code. Uber welcome discounts apply automatically once you create your account and book your first trip. Trust me, you’ll get used to the convenience of a rideshare app and a food and delivery service app, all in one place—in the palm of your hand.

According to recent reports, one of my go-to gifts lately is an Uber Eats gift card. I find it especially thoughtful and useful as a convenience gift, whether that’s after a death, loss, birth, or a major life change. An Uber Eats gift card is more than just a gift card. It takes another thing off someone’s plate and offers an easy, comforting meal, especially during times of grief or celebration. Uber Eats gift cards start at $15 and can be purchased from participating retailers or sent instantly through the app to friends and family.

In a recent development, being a student often means tight budgets, long nights, and limited kitchen space (and culinary knowledge). Investing in an Uber One account may be a good idea—for only $10 per month, you can get, on average, $30 in savings on Uber rides and Uber grocery and meal delivery. You won’t have to worry about meal planning or expensive takeout bills. With Uber One discounts and promos, you can get multiple meals for the week at a lower cost. And if you’re a student, you can try Uber One for free for four weeks to make sure the service is a fit. After that, the service is half off at only $5 per month. No Uber Eats coupon code necessary. Just verify your student status to get the four weeks for free and $5 per month after.

Sources indicate that if you’re not in the mood to eat out, stay in and get groceries delivered with Uber Eats. Uber Eats partners with hundreds of grocery stores near you—including your favorite supermarkets—for same-day delivery in as little as 25 minutes. Using your location, Uber Eats offers fast delivery from drugstores, grocery chains, and local stores, so whether you need toilet paper or a gallon of milk, Uber Eats delivers.

If you’re like me and need about 40 oz. of coffee to get through the day, you know how vital it is to have caffeine at a moment’s notice. With Uber Eats’ vast network, you can now get your Starbucks delivered. Starbucks delivery with Uber Eats couldn’t be easier. There are hundreds of Starbucks locations across the country, with both delivery and pickup available through the convenient app. Enter your zip code to see the nearest matching pickup location. Whether you’re catering for a substantial meeting or just want a quick breakfast.

If you’re an employer looking for an easy way to feed your workforce, consider Uber Eats. With Uber Eats catering, employees can enjoy the food they love while you keep costs and policies in check. Uber Eats for Business offers flexible meal programs for office lunches, late nights, and hybrid teams, all managed conveniently from one platform. Employees order what they want through Uber Eats, while your business gets clear visibility into spending and usage. Plus, where available, Uber One can help lower delivery costs on eligible orders.

It has been revealed that the government has declared that Alan Milburn has been appointed as chair of the fresh Youth Opportunities Unit mentioned by Pat McFadden earlier. (See 1.17pm.).

double quotation markAlan Milburn has been appointed as the chair of the new Youth Opportunities Unit.

The new unit will sit at the centre of government, reporting directly to the prime minister, driving the cross-system changes needed to deliver greater opportunities and support for young people ….

The responsibilities of the fresh unit are to:.

-Shaping and delivering the government response: Shaping and delivering the cross-government response to the Milburn review, maintaining an ambitious cross-system approach to reform and linking closely to the government’s wider agenda on growth, re-industrialisation and devolution.

-Unblocking delivery and driving progress: Unblocking delivery obstacles and supporting secretaries of state to drive progress towards reducing Neet rates.

-Guarantee, service design and devolution: Driving delivery of the Youth Opportunity and Support Guarantee and the Youth Opportunities Service, partnering with Number 10 North, departments, mayors, strategic and local authorities.

-Mobilising partners: Galvanising action beyond central government, working with mayors, securing commitments from employers and voluntary and community organisations, and demonstrating progress.

-Data, metrics and insight: Drawing on data and insight to understand what is and is not working, and addressing gaps in, or barriers to, data sharing to aid delivery.

Political figures who are given non-ministerial government roles often find that, in practice, they have a lot less power than they would like. Government is organised around departments, and within departments the secretary of state normally has the final say.

But the wording of this press release implies that Milburn could end up with considerable authority. If he is in charge of “unblocking delivery obstacles”, that will only happen if he is allowed to apply a robust approach towards “supporting” secretaries of state. This appointment will be seen as confirmation that Andy Burnham is fully committed to implementing this agenda.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for more than two decades, train commuters in Japan have had a faithful companion on their daily journeys: the Suica penguin. But the little black-and-white bird will soon take its last ride.

Sources indicate that one of Japan’s largest rail operators adopted the penguin as the mascot for its prepaid smart cards, known as Suica cards, in 2001. On the cards, the penguin is smiling and waving as it walks.

The East Japan Railway Firm, or JR East, announced the character’s retirement last year, and in September the company held an international public vote to pick a new mascot.

On Wednesday, the company will announce which latest character will replace the penguin. And in a country that loves its mascots, many people have strong opinions.

On Monday afternoon, at Sakuragicho railway station, southwest of Tokyo, customers at a store selling merchandise featuring the Suica penguin lamented the loss of a familiar presence.

It has been revealed that “I was really shocked when it was announced that the character would be ‘graduating,’” remarked Eriko Inoue, using JR East’s term for the outgoing penguin. Ms. Inoue, 50, a part-time nursery teacher, was stocking up on merchandise in case the organization discontinued some of it after the penguin’s retirement.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond in the upcoming film from director Denis Villeneuve.
  • Recent findings suggest that pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role.
  • According to recent reports, "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson stated in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond in the upcoming film from director Denis Villeneuve. It will be the 26th James Bond film and the first since Amazon MGM took over the iconic franchise.

Recent findings suggest that pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role. Monday's announcement — which came in part via an Instagram post — ends a long period of speculation about who would take over as "007" after Daniel Craig.

According to recent reports, "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson stated in a statement. "I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.".

According to recent reports, pattinson has appeared in several big-ticket films this year, including Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" and psychological thriller "Primetime," and he'll soon appear in "Dune: Part Three," also directed by Villeneuve. Pattinson, who rose to fame with the Twilight movie series, is also in production for Matt Reeves' "The Batman Part II," a follow-up to the 2022 film based on the DC comic.

The upcoming Bond film will have a script by Steven Knight and will be produced by Amy Pascal, known for her work on the Spider-Man franchise, and David Heyman, who produced all eight Harry Potter films.

It has been revealed that "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007," Villeneuve remarked. "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our upcoming James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.".

In 2022, Amazon bought MGM Studios, which had long produced the Bond movies, for roughly $8.45 billion. Amazon MGM then acquired creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights in 2025, when it closed a deal with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

The film is still untitled, and Amazon MGM hasn't confirmed a projected release date.

  • It was a nightmare trying to get the flights back to normal over the weekend, and then on Monday, United Airlines reported a system outage that they eventually rectified.
  • Industry observers note that chaos is the operative word for airlines these days, with near misses in the air, and increasing delays and cancellations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the incessant trouble in the airline industry reached a peak on Friday when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a rare nationwide ground stop, halting U.S. air traffic for more than four hours due to a critical telecommunications and network outage.

It was a nightmare trying to get the flights back to normal over the weekend, and then on Monday, United Airlines reported a system outage that they eventually rectified.

Industry observers note that chaos is the operative word for airlines these days, with near misses in the air, and increasing delays and cancellations. Amid all these industry pressures, United has another concern: The airline isn’t happy with passengers who rely on their AI chatbots to make reservations.

Industry observers note that first, let’s step back to just a few weeks ago, when United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby went on a podcast to brag about his latest personal breakthrough. After just three hour-long sessions with an AI tutor, the airline executive taught himself to "vibe-code" a custom sports-betting app, a tool designed to compare odds across platforms and automatically place bets on his behalf.

He called it an "AI epiphany." Apparently, that epiphany only applies when the guy running the airline is using AI to hunt for better odds.

Industry observers note that which raises a rather curious question in my mind. If the CEO of a major airline builds his own automated betting tool, does that come with any guardrails? Pro athletes get lifetime bans for wagering on their own games, so one has to hope Kirby’s vibe-coded bot isn't quietly placing action on prediction markets for "percentage of United flights delayed out of Newark.".

In a recent development, now, I’m not accusing the guy of shaving points on departure times (or an unexpected system outage), though it might explain a recent long delay I had flying out of Newark. All stated in fun, but I digress.

Recently, United updated its Contract of Carriage to explicitly ban third-party AI agents, like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse, from booking, changing, or managing flights on behalf of passengers.

Even if you're sitting right there supervising the transaction, United says that using a personal AI assistant to manage your trip is a no-go. Specifically, it means that United now classifies your reservation as a prohibited ticketing practice, giving the airline the legal right to cancel your trip without notice, confiscate your frequent flyer miles, and refuse to let you board.

Wow, sounds like United really, really hates it when you use AI. Which is odd, because the travel and hospitality industry — read United — has spent the last few years aggressively handing off reservation desks, customer support, and administrative jobs to AI.

It has been revealed that so, let me get this straight. Is United suddenly preaching the irreplaceable value of the human touch? The airline cited data security, the risk of "unintended purchases," and federal rules requiring passengers to personally attest during check-in that their bags don't contain explosives as reasons for opposing chatbot purchasing.

Sources indicate that OK, I get that. It makes sense. Well, sort of. Because, to me, what's actually happening here is that United isn't anti-AI. What I think United really means is, "Don't use AI, unless it's ours.".

If you've tried to rebook a canceled flight, dispute a baggage fee, or simply get a straight answer from an airline lately, you know how cumbersome the process is. You aren't talking to a human being. You're stuck in an endless loop with a clunky corporate chatbot or navigating an automated phone tree. Now, to be honest, have you ever done any of that successfully on your own without eventually having to speak with someone? The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Recent findings suggest that I didn't think so. I think the whole thing is actually designed to make you give up before reaching a real person.

Industry observers note that for years, major airlines, again, read United, have aggressively automated away human reservation desks, contact centers, and management roles in the name of efficiency. They're also using AI behind the scenes to track your habits and tweak ticket prices on the fly — pun intended. What they're trying to do is make sure you pay the absolute maximum you're willing to fork over.

In a recent development, the rise of agentic AI, bots that don't just summarize emails but actively browse the web, click buttons, and execute tasks for you, threatens to flip that behind-the-scenes tracking on its head. For the first time, regular people have access to automated tools that can finally fight bots with bots.

An AI agent working for you, and not the airline, doesn't get tired of refreshing flight pages to catch a $40 fare drop. It doesn't forget to apply your travel credits, and it won't cave to endless pop-ups begging you to pay extra for a carry-on bag or a seat assignment.

According to recent reports, worse yet, from an airline's perspective, a personal AI assistant strips away the airline's direct marketing funnel. As Kirby candidly admitted at an event in Chicago on Tuesday, "To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman.".

It has been revealed that for decades, airlines systematically cut commissions and squeezed out traditional human travel agents. I guess you could say they were the original "middlemen." Airlines hated paying someone else to advocate for the passenger.

Industry observers note that now, agentic AI is essentially giving every traveler a free digital travel agent. Why would airlines eliminate human travel agents just to let ChatGPT or Meta take their place?

And that brings us to the ultimate corporate double standard of the AI era.

When companies use AI to replace human booking agents, slash support staff, and jack up ticket prices, it's framed as "innovation." Workers lose their jobs, and customers are told to just deal with the bots left behind.

Yet the moment travelers deploy their own AI agents to hunt for cheaper fares, corporations slam the door shut, suddenly citing safety, compliance, and the sacred necessity of human involvement.

You can expect banks, retailers, and hotels to copy United's ban and continue replacing human workers with bots, all the while forcing shoppers to just deal with them.

In a recent development, until companies give back the human customer service they took away, banning our bots isn't really about protecting travelers. After all, as any guy with a custom sports-betting app knows, the real goal is making sure the house always wins.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Trump’s stopover at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit is part of a state visit to the Philippines, where he will be received with a 21-gun salute.

Industry observers note that the last time he met President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines, was full of praise for the Filipino leader.

“Great family, great family legacy and highly respected in his country,” Mr. Trump remarked while hosting Mr. Marcos at the White House last year.

Industry observers note that but that legacy was long considered an obstacle to Mr. Marcos’s political ambitions. He is the son of the dictator Ferdinand E. Marcos, who ruled the Philippines for 20 years, imposed martial law and was ousted in 1986 by a nonviolent uprising. The elder Marcos died in exile in Hawaii, without facing trial on U.S. criminal charges that he had plundered the Philippine Treasury. Years later, a court found his estate liable for torture, summary executions and disappearances.

According to recent reports, the younger Marcos spent years rehabilitating his family’s image and won election in 2022. He is hosting Mr. Trump at his official residence, Malacañang Palace, which was also his childhood home.

According to recent reports, mr. Marcos and his wife, Liza Marcos, will receive Mr. Trump on Wednesday with a 21-gun salute. Mr. Trump is expected to sign the palace guest book, hold closed-door meetings, pose for a handshake, then attend a state luncheon held in his honor.

In a recent development, it is not clear whether Mr. Trump, who has a well-known affinity for autocratic leaders, will meet with Mr. Marcos’s mother, Imelda, 97, with whom he has socialized in Latest York. Ms. Marcos wielded immense power when her husband was president and later came to be known for her flamboyant lifestyle, shoe collection and unexplained wealth.

Sources indicate that mr. Marcos has stated that when he called to congratulate Mr. Trump on his election victory in November 2024, Mr. Trump asked about Imelda Marcos.

According to recent reports, “My mother is really his friend, he knows my mother very well,” Mr. Marcos noted, relaying the conversation. “He was asking about her, ‘How’s Imelda?’ I told him she sends her congratulations.”.

Recent findings suggest that after the pomp and circumstance at Malacañang, which traces its roots to the Spanish colonial era in the Philippines, Mr. Trump is headed to Shenzhen, China. The highlight of that leg of his trip will be a trilateral meeting with two strongmen: President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia.

Breaking: The best MacBook to buy in 2026: Heres who should upgrade to the latest OLED MacBook Pro

💡 Key Takeaways
  • MacBooks have been ridiculously easy to recommend since we first started reviewing them in the mid-2010s, but especially since Apple rolled out its first M-series chips in 2020.
  • This fall, Apple launched two upcoming MacBook Pros — including its first with an OLED touchscreen display.
  • These are the tech, tools, and products — from laptops to e-readers, from earbuds to robovacs, and more — that Mashable ranks best in class.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MacBooks have been ridiculously easy to recommend since we first started reviewing them in the mid-2010s, but especially since Apple rolled out its first M-series chips in 2020. That custom silicon affords them much faster, quieter performance than most competing Windows PCs. When you factor in their elite build quality, beautiful displays, solid battery life, and polished operating system, it's little wonder that MacBooks are some of the most well-loved laptops.

This fall, Apple launched two upcoming MacBook Pros — including its first with an OLED touchscreen display. After hands-on testing the entire current lineup, these are the best MacBooks we recommend for different kinds of users.

These are the tech, tools, and products — from laptops to e-readers, from earbuds to robovacs, and more — that Mashable ranks best in class.

The 15-inch M5 MacBook Air is the best MacBook for most people. It's a sleek, future-proofed ultraportable with the right amount of premium features and more than enough muscle for everyday multitasking, including occasional content creation. It's the ideal daily driver.

You might also consider the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air, which is slightly cheaper and more portable. We think it's the best MacBook for college students.

The MacBook Neo is our top pick for budget shoppers, casual users, and younger students. It's not nearly as fast or as fancy as a MacBook Air, but it's a good performer for its price point, and it's just as well-made as any other MacBook. If your typical workload involves bopping between some Chrome tabs and an app or two, look no further.

The 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro is our upgrade pick for power owners with consistently heavy workloads and a moderate amount of wiggle room in their budgets. (Realistically, it's the best MacBook Pro for most people.) The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The only people who should splurge on the new touch-enabled MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display are professional creatives who primarily use their computer for intensive visual and design work. We recommend going with the 16-inch model for the maximum screen space — its tandem OLED display is just that good.

Apple raised the prices of all of its MacBooks this summer — thanks, RAMageddon — and the upcoming MacBook Pros are quite expensive. Even the M6 base model costs $2,000. If you're mulling an upgrade, be sure to keep a close eye on Black Friday sales: Most retailers save their most competitive MacBook deals for the year-end holiday season.

Sources indicate that here are the Black Friday MacBook deals we expect to see in the coming weeks, based on our coverage of last year's sales and, in the case of the MacBook Neo, our wishful thinking. (The Neo wasn't around for Black Friday 2025, but it's due for a discount of at least $50 at this point in its lifecycle.).

For a deeper dive into all of our best MacBook picks, read on.

Apple's latest MacBook Air packs the snappy performance of the M5 chip inside a predictably polished and portable design. It's a great daily driver that can do basically anything the average person needs a laptop for, making it the best MacBook for everyday use. Yes, it's several hundred dollars pricier than a MacBook Neo, but it's a much better, more future-proofed computer in every way.

Recent findings suggest that I think most folks will make good use of the larger screen on the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air, which starts at $1,499. It's configurable with up to 32GB of RAM and up to 4TB of storage.

Read Mashable's full review of the 15-inch Apple MacBook Air (M5).

Industry observers note that the M5 MacBook Air successfully beats the awkward middle child allegations. It easily handles the workloads of everyday multitaskers, and it has some premium features that won't feel outdated in a few years (without going too overboard on nice-to-haves).

Performance-wise, this is one of the fastest laptops on the market no matter how you stack it. It zips through simpler single-core tasks like web browsing, and isn't intimidated by heavy multi-core workloads like video editing. Just be mindful that too much of the latter can make it warm and cause thermal throttling — it's fanless, after all. The MacBook Pros have fans, so they're better at handling the stress of creative apps and games over longer periods of time.

The M5 MacBook Air lasted 17 hours and 40 minutes in our battery life benchmark, which is a video rundown test. That's a small downgrade from the last generation, but you won't be screwed if you forget your charger at home.

According to recent reports, aesthetically, this is largely the same laptop as the M4 MacBook Air, which isn't a terrible thing, since that laptop slapped. (It just makes for a boring gen-over-gen update.) It has a crisp 12MP Center Stage webcam, a vivid Liquid Retina display, amazing speakers, a luxe haptic trackpad, a snappy backlit Magic Keyboard with Touch ID, and a sleek all-aluminum design. Like all MacBooks, its build quality is class-leading. You can take your pick from four neutral finishes: sky blue, silver, starlight, and midnight.

Sources indicate that for its ultraportable design and slightly lower price tag, I deem the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air the best MacBook for college students — particularly liberal arts, humanities, nursing, and social science majors. (Your coursework probably doesn't require Windows.) The budget MacBook Neo can serve you well in the short term if you just need a basic laptop for writing essays and sending emails. But this compact Air is a smarter investment that will last you past graduation.

As a college student, you'll save $100 on the 13-inch MacBook Air with Apple's education discount. It starts at $1,199 with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, which you can bump up to 32GB and 4TB, respectively.

Sources indicate that read PCMag's full review of the 13-inch Apple MacBook Air (M5). PCMag and Mashable are both owned by Ziff Davis.

The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is just as fast and pretty as the 15-inch model, but easier to carry across campus (and a little nicer on your wallet).

There are only a couple minor differences between the two sizes. The 13-incher has two fewer speakers, and its base model has a lesser GPU with two fewer cores (eight versus 10), making it a hair worse for stuff like light video editing and gaming. Otherwise, their performance and specs are identical. It comes in the same four colorways, too.

Recent findings suggest that the MacBook Neo is the best choice for budget buyers and casual users, including K-12 students. It's not as well-rounded as a MacBook Air, but it's an amazing starter laptop with the same great build quality (and livelier color options). It also makes a good secondary laptop for entertainment and online shopping if your daily driver lives at the office.

The MacBook Neo comes in two configurations. There's a $699 base model with 256GB of storage, and a $799 version that doubles your disk space and adds Touch ID.

Read Mashable's full review of the Apple MacBook Neo.

The Neo doesn't have a ton of pizzazz or multitasking brawn, but it's great for what it is: a very cheap MacBook. It outclasses most similarly priced Windows laptops and Chromebooks.

Recent findings suggest that inside the Neo, you'll find an A18 Pro chip with a six-core CPU and a five-core GPU, which is a lesser version of the processor inside 2024's iPhone 16 Pro. A laptop running on a smartphone chip? How does that work? Very well, actually, per our benchmarking. (Modern smartphones have been holding their own against PCs for some time now.) In basic single-core tasks, the Neo scores on par with an M4 MacBook Air. In other words, it feels just as snappy as a much more expensive MacBook when you're browsing the web, sending emails, and streaming videos.

In heavy multi-core tasks like video editing, the Neo scores about as well as an M1 MacBook Air from 2020 — not too shabby. Mashable tech editor Timothy Beck Werth had no trouble using it for a simple Final Cut Pro edit. But keep in mind that its 8GB of fixed RAM is really going to limit your ability to juggle a bunch of apps or files. The archetypal Neo user will only have a couple of browser tabs open at any given time, maybe with Spotify running in the background. Anything too demanding will make it pokey.

According to recent reports, the Neo lasts for around 15 hours per charge. It dies much sooner than an Air or Pro, but it'll definitely get you through a full workday with plenty of juice to spare.

The 13-inch Neo weighs the same as a 13-inch MacBook Air (which technically measures 13.6 inches across), but it's slightly thicker. It's also fanless, just like the Air. It has a pretty Liquid Retina display and excellent speakers with Dolby Atmos and Spatial Audio support. Its 1080p webcam is located in its upper bezel, so unlike a MacBook Air or base Pro, it doesn't have an uggo notch jutting down into its screen. Apple ditched features like keyboard backlighting, True Tone display technology, a haptic touchpad, and fast Thunderbolt ports in making the Neo affordable, but it didn't skimp on build quality. It has an all-aluminum design that makes it just as sturdy and polished as any other MacBook. (Most cheap laptops have plastic components.) It also comes in some fun colors like blush, citrus, and indigo.

The M6 MacBook Pro is our top pick for power people who are willing to pay a little extra for a smoother, brighter display, more ports, better speakers, and more sustained computing power. It's overkill for the average person, but it's worth the investment for most content creators, developers, AI enthusiasts, and other professionals who run demanding creative apps (plus the occasional game) on a regular basis.

The M6 MacBook Pro is available in one 14-inch size starting at $1,999 with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. It maxes out with 32GB of RAM and 4TB of disk space. You can upgrade its display with a nano-texture (matte) finish for $150 extra.

Read Mashable's full review of the 14-inch Apple MacBook Pro (M6).

Some users will look at the M5 MacBook Air and find its specs a little lacking — more "adequate" than "amazing." For you, there's the M6 MacBook Pro.

It has been revealed that the MacBook Air's M5 chip is no slouch by any means, but this guy's fresher M6 chip is even more powerful, especially in demanding multi-core workloads. And its fans make it better at handling them over a long period of time; thermal throttling is much more likely with an Air.

Industry observers note that it's worth mentioning that Mashable's Timothy Beck Werth was able to play Cyberpunk 2077 on the M6 MacBook Pro at 30fps. I wouldn't buy it solely for this reason: Windows laptops are compatible with way more games than MacBooks, and PCs with discrete GPUs, especially, are much better-equipped to run graphically taxing titles. But just know that AAA gaming is possible here if you want to run the occasional mission after work.

Design-wise, the M6 MacBook Pro is slightly less portable than the Air, but not by much. It's less than 0.2 inches thicker than both sizes and 0.1 pounds heavier than the 15-inch model. This affords it enough room for extra fixings like an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, and a bonus Thunderbolt port, as well as an awesome hi-fi sound system with force-cancelling woofers. I've tested dozens of laptops over the course of my career, and none of them sound better than a MacBook Pro.

The M5 MacBook Pro looks as spectacular as it sounds, as per tradition. (Apple hasn't made any drastic design changes to it since 2021.) Compared to the M5 MacBook Air's standard Liquid Retina screen, its mini-LED "Liquid Retina XDR" display is crisper, brighter, and smoother when displaying visuals in motion. Take your pick from two finishes: space black or silver. Be mindful that the former is a fingerprint magnet.

We haven't run our battery life test on the M6 MacBook Pro yet, but we have high expectations. Last year's M5 model held out for 21 hours and 17 minutes to become the longest-lasting MacBook we've ever tried.

Recent findings suggest that apple's all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is geared toward deep-pocketed creative professionals whose work requires a ton of horsepower and a reference-quality display. (And, to a lesser extent, people who've missed MacBooks' glowing Apple logo, which hasn't been a thing since 2015.).

Recent findings suggest that this beastly machine comes in a 14-inch size (starting at $2,899) and a 16-inch size (starting at $3,399) with an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip, 24GB to 128GB of RAM, and 1TB to 16TB of SSD storage. Both can be upgraded with a nano-texture display finish. We prefer the bigger model for the extra screen space.

Read Mashable's full review of the 16-inch Apple MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display (M5 Pro).

It has been revealed that its name is a mouthful, and its screen is an eyeful. Apple's all-newly introduced MacBook Pro has an elite tandem OLED display that wowed Mashable Tech Editor Timothy Beck Werth. "Apple hasn't just made an OLED laptop; it's made a genuine reference-quality display, designed to meet industry standards for video editors, photographers, animators, 3D artists, and color graders," he wrote. ("Reference-quality" refers to the fact that its colors are extremely lifelike and accurate.) It's an absolutely luscious display — not to mention super bright. It can hit up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR brightness, which makes it one of the brightest laptop displays ever made.

It has been revealed that the fresh MacBook Pro's OLED display has touch capabilities, too, which is mainly interesting because it brings support for the Dynamic Island instead of a webcam notch. (And Apple execs' history of hating on touchscreen laptops, of course.) You can't use it as a tablet, nor does it support styluses. "If I were a betting man, I would wager that the touchscreen won't stick around forever," Werth stated.

Industry observers note that the model we tested ran on the M5 Pro, and our benchmarking showed that it's a macho, macho chip. In multi-core tasks, it whizzes past every laptop processor we've ever tried — in any MacBook or Windows PC. Compared to the M6 chip in the new base MacBook Pro, it offers a jaw-dropping 57 percent performance boost when running intensive software.

What's even more impressive is the fact that the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display doesn't heat up easily, despite being thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pros. The 16-inch model weighs in at four pounds — a whopping 0.7 pounds less than its non-OLED counterpart, which makes a real difference when you're working on the go.

Recent findings suggest that the other main design differences between this model and the standard MacBook Pro are its glowing Apple logo and upgraded sound system, which "[provides] deeper bass and better clarity," Werth said. Their keyboards, trackpads, color options, webcams, mics, and port setups are the same.

Our battery life test results for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display aren't finalized yet, but Apple rated it at up to 24 hours of video streaming (same as the regular Pro).

Recent findings suggest that in November 2026, I added two newly introduced picks based on our latest round of testing. The M6 MacBook Pro is now our upgrade pick, and the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is our new top pick for professional creatives. (Look for their battery life test results in the next upgrade.) I also added information about Black Friday MacBook deals.

In August 2026, I updated this guide to reflect Apple's newly increased MacBook prices and named the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air our top pick for college students.

In May 2026, I added the results of our battery life testing for the M5 MacBook Air. It was able to loop a video for 17 hours and 40 minutes before dying.

MacBooks tend to go on sale at their deepest discounts during Amazon's summer Prime Day sale and around Black Friday. They also see steep price cuts as soon as they're no longer current-generation models, meaning right after Apple introduces their successors (which usually happens every year in March and October.).

Apple hosts a Black Friday sale every year, but it just entails free gift card promotions. For proper price cuts, shop around at third-party retailers like Amazon and Best Buy.

In a recent development, first, a little info about how Apple classifies its older products. Devices that it stopped selling more than five years ago but less than seven are considered "vintage," whereas devices it stopped selling more than seven years ago are "obsolete.".

Vintage MacBooks are still eligible for hardware support from Apple, depending on parts availability, but it won't fix obsolete MacBooks. And you can't get parts for them from third-party service providers like Best Buy and Micro Center.

According to recent reports, if your obsolete MacBook is still chugging along like normal, is in good condition, and doesn't seem sluggish or scant on storage, by all means, keep using it. However, if any component breaks, deteriorates, or no longer meets your needs, it's time to send it off to the great MacBook farm in the sky. Consider recycling or donating it so it doesn't sit in a landfill.

While MacBooks don't get software updates forever, it's not a dealbreaker if yours can't run the latest version of macOS. You might be able to repurpose it as a streaming device or turn it into a Chromebook. That noted, a MacBook you use as your primary laptop for school or work needs to be compatible with the current macOS in order to stay secure and continue running Apple apps.

FYI: The latest version of Apple's Mac operating system, macOS 27 (aka macOS Golden Gate), only works with M-series MacBooks from 2020 or later. That means if your daily driver is an older model with an Intel chip, it's high time to upgrade. It will still get security updates for the next two-ish years but won't support any latest features going forward.

According to recent reports, some of the best Windows laptops and Chromebooks we've tested can rival MacBooks on performance and/or build quality. My favorite MacBook alternatives include the Asus Zenbook A14, the Dell XPS 13, and the Dell XPS 14.

If you want to stay within the Apple ecosystem, iPads also make good MacBook alternatives thanks to iPadOS's "windowing" system.

It has been revealed that mashable has been writing about laptops for over a decade, and I've personally been covering them since 2023. I also helped develop the rigorous hands-on testing process we right now use to review them. This methodology revolves around four criteria:.

Sources indicate that the laptops we review get put to work as our primary computers. This includes trying any unique software or use cases they support. We also subject all of our loaners to a multi-app/tab stress test and Primate Labs' Geekbench, which measures CPU performance in common tasks. Gaming laptops get put through additional graphical benchmarking.

Industry observers note that to gauge a laptop's stamina, we conduct a battery rundown test that involves playing a looped 1080p version of "Tears of Steel," a short open-source Blender movie, at 50 percent brightness and 50 percent volume. Ideally, we hope to get at least 19 hours of battery life from MacBooks.

As we're using a laptop, we zero in on certain components to evaluate its build quality. These include the display, keyboard, touchpad, webcam, speakers, and ports. We also assess its overall aesthetic and portability.

We determine the ultimate value of a laptop by comparing its performance, design/build quality, and battery life to other laptops with similar pricing, specs, release dates, and use cases. We consider any accessories it comes with, any upgrades from its predecessor(s), and its future-proofing.

Haley Henschel is a Chicago-based Senior Shopping Reporter at Mashable who reviews and finds deals on popular tech, from laptops to gaming consoles and VPNs. She has years of experience covering shopping holidays and can tell you what’s actually worth buying on Black Friday and Amazon Prime Day. Her work has also explored the driving forces behind digital trends within the shopping sphere, from dupes to 12-foot skeletons.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Exclusive: Parents of Chloe Moffat urge employers to treat staff facing allegations in a kinder, more human way.
  • The parents of a Treasury worker who took her own life last year have launched a policy that directs employers to treat staff in a kinder and more commonsense way, and are asking HR departments across the country to adopt it.
  • Chloe Moffat’s parents also stated the government department prepares to plant a memorial garden in her honour at its Horse Guards Road offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Exclusive: Parents of Chloe Moffat urge employers to treat staff facing allegations in a kinder, more human way.

The parents of a Treasury worker who took her own life last year have launched a policy that directs employers to treat staff in a kinder and more commonsense way, and are asking HR departments across the country to adopt it.

Chloe Moffat’s parents also stated the government department prepares to plant a memorial garden in her honour at its Horse Guards Road offices.

Moffat, a 26-year-old personal assistant, took her own life the day after she was called into a surprise disciplinary meeting about anonymous complaints alleging she had disclosed sensitive information at work, which she denied. A coroner found in August that the Treasury had “materially contributed” to her death.

She had been convinced she would lose her job, the coroner heard, despite that not being a likely outcome. Moffat’s managers declined to allow her to bring a colleague to the “informal” meeting, did not give her any advance notice of it and refused to tell her whether she was likely to lose her job. They also removed access to her director’s email and changed her work responsibilities.

She had worked at the Treasury for almost three years, loved her job and had an exemplary employment record, the coroner heard.

It has been revealed that her parents, Anne and David Moffat, have been working with the Global Kindness Institute, an NGO, to come up with “Chloe’s policy” for HR departments to adopt to prevent such tragic incidents from happening in future. They are calling on organisations across the country to help develop and take on the policy.

According to recent reports, “All we want is for nobody else to go through this,” Anne Moffat said. “If it goes through HR departments, even people considering making allegations, everybody can hopefully follow the Chloe policy and ask if this is really necessary.

“So many people are so policy driven and so into disciplinaries and making people accountable when it may not be necessary. People aren’t being treated in a commonsense, human way.”.

The policy calls on HR departments to consider the harms of disciplinary processes to those subjected to them, particularly when complaints are anonymous or unverified. It emphasises prioritising psychological safety and supporting those going through any disciplinary process, as well as minimising these processes in the first place by considering alternatives. It also calls on HR departments to provide clarity to those going through disciplinary processes, including letting people know if their role is safe.

David Moffat noted: “It’s a powerful leadership standard. If it raises the profile of the process that Chloe went through and avoids it happening to anyone else, that is good enough for me.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Treasury’s response to the coroner’s prevention of future deaths report acknowledged the department’s role in her death and committed to safeguards. A review of the civil service by the Cabinet Office found that the conditions to which Moffat was subjected had been replicated in other disciplinary meetings.

Anne Moffat said: “If you think about what happened to Chloe, if HR had thought ‘we know that she was very well thought of, nothing else had ever happened, these were the first ever allegations, they were anonymous,’ was this process necessary?”.

The prevention of future deaths report issued by the coroner last month found there was still a risk at the civil service due to its disciplinary procedures. The civil service has put in place multiple safeguards to address these concerns. This guidance includes allowing staff to have a supporter in disciplinary meetings, giving proper notice of any such meeting, and informing staff if a dismissal is not likely. The Treasury is also hiring an on-site occupational therapist to support staff wellbeing.

The Moffats met James Bowler, the permanent secretary at the Treasury, at the end of last month. David remarked: “We felt listened to, and as part of their response to the coroner as well we felt reassured that change was being implemented. If the changes they have put forward to the coroner had already been in place, we certainly feel that Chloe would be with us today. It was a very emotional meeting.”.

According to recent reports, anne added: “It is the first time we felt that the Treasury had been compassionate to us and it wasn’t defensive or legal speak. They are looking at how to remember Chloe, and looking at the possibility of a memorial garden within the building and marking the garden with a plaque.”.

David said: “We feel that Chloe is finally being acknowledged and remembered.”.

A Treasury spokesperson said: “The Treasury’s deepest sympathies continue to be with Chloe’s friends and family, and the department continues to mourn our colleague.

“Our response to the coroner’s prevention of future deaths report sets out the action we have taken following this tragic case. An independent review found staff acted in good faith and with a duty of care throughout.”.

A latest approach to a Covid-19 nasal vaccine highlights early promise

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1460 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scientists in Germany say they’ve been able to make a nasal vaccine that can shut down a Covid-19 infection in the nose and throat, where the virus gets its first foothold in the body.
  • In experiments in hamsters, two doses of the vaccine – which is made with a live but weakened form of the coronavirus that causes Covid-19 – blocked the virus from copying itself in the animals’ upper airways, achieving “sterilizing immunity” and preventing illness, a long-sought goal of the pandemic.
  • WHO experts revise Covid-19 vaccine advice, say healthy kids and teens low risk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientists in Germany say they’ve been able to make a nasal vaccine that can shut down a Covid-19 infection in the nose and throat, where the virus gets its first foothold in the body.

In experiments in hamsters, two doses of the vaccine – which is made with a live but weakened form of the coronavirus that causes Covid-19 – blocked the virus from copying itself in the animals’ upper airways, achieving “sterilizing immunity” and preventing illness, a long-sought goal of the pandemic.

WHO experts revise Covid-19 vaccine advice, say healthy kids and teens low risk.

Although this vaccine has several more hurdles to clear before it gets to a doctor’s office or drug store, other nasal vaccines are in use or are nearing the finish line in clinical trials.

China and India both rolled out vaccines given through the nasal tissues last fall, though it’s not clear how well they may be working. Studies on the effectiveness of these vaccines have yet to be published, leaving much of the world to wonder whether this approach to protection really works in people.

In a recent development, the US has reached something of a stalemate with Covid-19. Even with the darkest days of the pandemic behind us, hundreds of Americans are still dying daily as the infection continues to simmer in the background of our return to normal life.

As long as the virus continues to spread among people and animals, there’s always the potential for it mutate into a more contagious or more damaging version of itself. And while Covid infections have become manageable for most healthy people, they may still pose a danger to vulnerable groups such as the elderly and immunocompromised.

Researchers hope next-generation Covid-19 vaccines, which aim to shut down the virus before it ever gets a chance to make us sick and ultimately prevent the spread of infection, could make our newest resident respiratory infection less of a threat.

China approves its first mRNA Covid-19 vaccine.

One way scientists are trying to do that is by boosting mucosal immunity, beefing up immune defenses in the tissues that line the upper airways, right where the virus would land and begin to infect our cells.

It’s a bit like stationing firefighters underneath the smoke alarm in your house, says study author Emanuel Wyler, a scientist at the Max Delbruck Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association in Berlin.

The immunity that’s created by shots works throughout the body, but it resides primarily in the blood. That means it may take longer to mount a response.

“If they are already on site, they can immediately eliminate the fire, but if they’re like 2 miles away, they first need to drive there, and by that time, one-third of the house is already in full flames,” Wyler said.

Mucosal vaccines are also better at priming a different kind of first responder than injections do. They do a better job of summoning IgA antibodies, which have four arms to grab onto invaders instead of the two arms that the y-shaped IgG antibodies have. Some scientists think IgA antibodies may be less picky about their targets than IgG antibodies, which makes them better equipped to deal with fresh variants.

The new nasal vaccine takes a new approach to a very old idea: weakening a virus so it’s no longer a threat and then giving it to people so their immune systems can learn to recognize and fight it off. The first vaccines using this approach date to the 1870s, against anthrax and rabies. Back then, scientists weakened the agents they were using with heat and chemicals.

The researchers manipulated the genetic material in the virus to make it harder for cells to translate. This technique, called codon pair deoptimization, hobbles the virus so it can be shown to the immune system without making the body sick.

According to recent reports, “You could imagine reading a text … and every letter is a different font, or every letter is a different size, then the text is much harder to read. And this is basically what we do in codon pair deoptimization,” Wyler said.

In the hamster studies, which were published Monday in the journal Nature Microbiology, two doses of the live but weakened nasal vaccine created a much stronger immune response than either two doses of an mRNA-based vaccine or one that uses an adenovirus to ferry the vaccine instructions into cells.

The researchers think the live weakened vaccine probably worked better because it closely mimics the process of a natural infection.

The nasal vaccine also previews the entire coronavirus for the body, not just its spike proteins like current Covid-19 vaccines do, so the hamsters were able to make immune weapons against a wider range of targets.

Recent findings suggest that as promising as all this sounds, vaccine experts say caution is warranted. This vaccine still has to pass more tests before it’s ready for use, but they say the results look encouraging.

Health officials consider another round of bivalent boosters for the most vulnerable Americans.

Sources indicate that “They did a very nice job. This is obviously a competent and thoughtful team that did this work, and impressive in the scope of what they did. Now it just needs to be repeated,” perhaps in primates and certainly in humans before it can be widely used, stated Dr. Greg Poland, who designs vaccines at the Mayo Clinic. He was not involved in the new research.

Sources indicate that the study began in 2021, before the Omicron variant was around, so the vaccine tested in these experiments was made with the original strain of the coronavirus. In the experiments, when they infected animals with Omicron, the live but weakened nasal vaccine still performed better than the others, but its ability to neutralize the virus was diminished. Researchers think it will need an revision.

It also needs to be tested in humans, and Wyler indicates they’re working on that. The scientists have partnered with a Swiss firm called RocketVax to start phase I clinical trials.

Sources indicate that other vaccines are further along, but the progress has been “slow and halting,” Poland noted. Groups working on these vaccines are struggling to raise the steep costs of getting a new vaccine to market, and they’re doing it in a setting where people tend to think the vaccine race has been won and done.

According to recent reports, in reality, Poland noted, we’re far from that. All it would take is another Omicron-level shift in the evolution of the virus, and we could be back at square one, with no effective tools against the coronavirus.

“That’s foolish. We should be developing a pan-coronavirus vaccine that does induce mucosal immunity and that is long-lived,” he said.

At least four nasal vaccines for Covid-19 have reached late-stage testing in people, according to the World Health Organization’s vaccine tracker.

The nasal vaccines in use in China and India rely on harmless adenoviruses to ferry their instructions into cells, although effectiveness data for these has not been published.

Two other nasal vaccines are finishing human studies.

Covid vaccine maker Novavax says it may not survive.

One, a recombinant vaccine that can be produced cheaply in chicken eggs, the same way many flu vaccines are, is being put through its paces by researchers at Mount Sinai in Upcoming York City.

Another, like the German vaccine, uses a live but weakened version of the virus. It’s being developed by a company called Codagenix. Results of those studies, which were carried out in South America and Africa, may come later this year.

The German team states it’s eagerly watching for the Codagenix data.

“They will be very vital in order to know where whether this kind of attempt is basically promising or not,” Wyler mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that they have reason to worry. Respiratory infections have proved to be tough targets for inhaled vaccines.

FluMist, a live but weakened form of the flu virus, works reasonably well in children but doesn’t help adults as much. The reason is thought to be that adults already have immune memory for the flu, and when the virus is injected into the nose, the vaccine mostly boosts what’s already there.

Still, some of the most potent vaccines such as the vaccine against measles, mumps and rubella use live attenuated viruses, so it’s a promising approach.

Industry observers note that another consideration is that live vaccines can’t be taken by everyone. People with very compromised immunity are often cautioned against using live vaccines because even these very weakened viruses may be risky for them.

“Although it’s strongly attenuated, it’s still a real virus,” Wyler stated, so it would have to be used carefully.

JPMorgan Chase reported a "technical issue" that was affecting some consumer banking services Monday.

The bank mentioned a "temporary problem related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" was causing some customer transactions to take longer than usual, though it said customers can still access their accounts and funds.

"There is no evidence it is cyber-related," a JPMorgan spokesperson stated in a statement to CNBC.

According to recent reports, "This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson remarked. "We're working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today.".

CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved.

Recent findings suggest that still, other major banks were listed in outage reports as transactions between Chase and other institutions appeared to get held up. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET.

A representative for U.S. Bank mentioned that tech giant was "not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.".

Zelle is the peer-to-peer payments system backed by many of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan.

The outage reports come days after separate, widespread issues with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers.

— CNBC's Leslie Picker contributed to this report.
